items.title: A summer in Dublin
sentences: Marta has wanted to study English abroad for years, and this summer she finally booked a course in Dublin.
The course lasts four weeks, and she will live with a local family during that time.
She is a little nervous about this, because she has never stayed with strangers before.
Her teacher, Mr Hughes, tells her not to worry, however: most host families are very kind, and the first dinner is the hardest part.
If he is right, Marta will be chatting in English at breakfast within a few days.
By the end of the course, she hopes to be thinking in English instead of translating in her head.

explanation.en: 'The course' repeats 'a course' (a becomes the). 'This' points to living with a family, 'however' answers her worry, 'he' is Mr Hughes, and the last sentence looks ahead to the end of the course.
explanation.es: 'The course' repite 'a course' (a pasa a the). 'This' remite a vivir con una familia, 'however' contesta a su preocupación, 'he' es Mr Hughes y la última frase mira al final del curso.

note.es: A course pasa a ser the course.

note.en: It means living with a local family.
note.es: Se refiere a vivir con una familia local.

note.en: The teacher says the opposite of what worries her.
note.es: El profesor dice lo contrario de lo que la preocupa.

note.en: It looks ahead to the end of the four weeks.
note.es: Mira al final de las cuatro semanas.

items.title: Studying smarter
sentences: Many first-year students arrive at university convinced that long hours in the library are the key to good grades.
Research on learning, however, suggests that this belief is only partly true.
What matters more is how the time is spent, and in particular whether students test themselves rather than simply rereading their notes.
This habit, known as retrieval practice, helps people to remember information far longer than rereading does.
As a result, a number of universities now run short workshops in which new students are taught how to apply it.
The workshops are usually optional, so the students who would benefit most are not always the ones who attend.

explanation.en: 'This belief' sums up the opening idea. 'The time' means the long hours, 'This habit' is testing yourself, 'As a result' and 'it' lead to the workshops, and 'The workshops' repeats 'workshops' (a general noun becomes a known one).
explanation.es: 'This belief' resume la idea inicial. 'The time' son las largas horas, 'This habit' es autoevaluarse, 'As a result' e 'it' llevan a los talleres y 'The workshops' retoma 'workshops'.

note.en: It sums up the idea that long hours mean good grades.
note.es: Resume la idea de que muchas horas dan buenas notas.

note.en: The hours spent in the library.
note.es: Las horas pasadas en la biblioteca.

note.en: Universities react to what research shows.
note.es: Las universidades reaccionan a lo que muestra la investigación.
Workshops pasa a ser the workshops.
